# AST pure safety review R1

Verdict: no additional actionable finding against the frozen source.

Reviewed the quality freeze at `/root/.local/state/rust-ast-pure-20261026-ofw__fhw/source`, not the live workspace. `artifacts/quality-receipt.json` records `success: true` and `phase: quality`. Its `source_hashes` for the evaluator, pure module, registry, context, vm, value, and `tests/fixtures/ast_pure_cases.json` (`aa23a7547c376e48b728bbc1cca8601dba2a4d824b15c2ac30e0a3ea7df7da44`) match `snapshot.json`. Pure dispatch already contains the mechanical fix `parse_int(checked_string(value)?.as_ref())` at `pure/mod.rs:63`. This review did not run Rust, Cargo, rustfmt, or a timed benchmark. The generic-constant mirror and release bench were still outstanding when this report was written.

Lead-reported quality, not re-executed here: 339 passing executions (87 lib, 13 old, 10 pure, 2 doc, 129 combined, 13 old, 10 pure, 62 old lib, 13 old integration), full 4,694 pure cases twice, and the old 3,554 supported cases plus 9 boundaries across 3 profiles. Checks, Clippy, and four worker graphs passed in that run.

## Out of scope for a new finding

The ordinary `toString` throw, array and cycle `String()` traversal, slice’s invalid-start tail, full filter coercion, replace’s pre-empty coercion, and random’s throw-before-draw are implemented in `pure/coercion.rs`, `pure/strings.rs`, `pure/user.rs`, and `pure/mod.rs`. The 4,694-case pass covers them. They are not re-filed.

`count` still uses infallible `js_string` after it selects the raw effective argument (`registry.rs` builtin). That is the required old coercer. Private `checked_string` stays `pub(super)` inside `pure/`.

## Typed context

`user_display_name: String` and `argument: Option<JsString>` stay the nominal fields. `effective_user_display_name` and `effective_argument` return `argument_override` / `user_display_name_override` unchanged when `Some`, including `Some(Null)` and `Some(0)`. `None` uses the nominal field. Snapshot timer context and the bench scalar projection read those accessors.

Consumers:

- `user` / `touser` read the accessors. A truthy raw display is returned as itself when no filter applies. A falsy display falls through to `user_login`. Event-data names still go through `checked_string`. `touser` escapes only real strings; other truthy values use `checked_string` and are not escaped. Corpus cases `pure-user-fallback-1981` through `1983` and `pure-touser-fallback-2150` are null display or argument, then the login string. Null is falsy, so the stale nominal string is not consulted.
- `count` selects `args[0]` or `effective_argument()` with `js_truthy`, then `js_string`. It does not stringify inside the accessor.
- Command-ref `chatter_user_name` uses `effective_user_display_name()`. A truthy value is stored raw. A falsy value stores the login string, which already falls back to `broadcaster_id` when login is empty. The previous empty-string check on the nominal field is gone.

`JsValue::get` changed in one place: the key compare no longer builds `JsString::from(key)`. It compares stored units to `key.encode_utf16()`. The argument is a Rust `&str`, so both sides are the UTF-16 encoding of valid Unicode. Lone-surrogate keys cannot appear. Observed diff versus baseline is that single line. Inferred: lookup results are unchanged. The compare does not allocate a key buffer.

## Focus checks

Observed with Node 26.8.2 (`quality-receipt.json` reference node v26.8.2, ICU 78.3, Unicode 17.0) unless noted.

Unicode 17 additions. The `LETTER` / `MARK` / `NUMBER` regexes are `\p{L|M|N}` plus the explicit ranges in `/tmp/ast-pure-unicode-delta.json`. Those ranges match the delta exactly: L 4,644, M 42, N 13. Every added scalar is that category in Node, and none is also another of L/M/N. This review did not re-walk regex-syntax 0.8.11’s `LETTER`/`MARK`/`NUMBER` tables; the registry extract was not readable on the later probe. No missing or extra scalar versus Unicode 16 was re-derived here. Inferred from the crate header seen earlier in the same freeze: those tables are Unicode 16.0.0, which is why the unions exist.

Casing. ASCII fast path runs only when every unit is below 128 and only shifts A–Z / a–z. Node `toLowerCase` sources whose lowercase is a single ASCII letter, for the letters that appear in the filter words, are only those ASCII letters. Sampled Node results match the Rust unit-test literals: `"ßﬃ".toUpperCase()` is `SSFFI`, `"ΟΣ İ".toLowerCase()` is `ος` plus `i` + U+0307, title of `foo-BAR !HELLO` + U+FEFF + `ßETA` is `Foo-bar !hello` + U+FEFF + `SSeta`, and capitalize of `𐐨abc` leaves the first unit unchanged. U+0085 stays in place and does not open a new title word. U+FEFF, U+000B, and U+2028 do. That matches `js_compat::is_whitespace`, which excludes U+0085. Lone surrogates are outside the ASCII fast path. Fast-versus-generic equality and the `>=5%` ASCII gate were not re-measured here.

Filter tokens. An exhaustive Node scan found no code point whose `toLowerCase()` is `ignore`, `symbols`, or `numbers`, and no one-character substitution whose lowercase equals those words while failing the ASCII fold. `token_eq` matches `toLowerCase` for those three words. `Object.hasOwn` rejects any other token, including prototype names. The implementation coerces every argument before it returns, including after an unknown token.

User iteration. Node `for-of` plus the source regexes on `["A!","B2","\u0301"]` with both filters returns `A!` + U+0301. Removing the digit between U+D800 and U+DC00 leaves U+10000. `/\p{L}/u.test("\uD800")` is false and does not throw. The frozen corpus has zero cases whose expected text contains `not iterable`.

Random and numbers. `checked_string` runs before `host.random`. Falsy input skips coercion and uses 100. `parse_int` is the existing base-10 parser; `|| 100` is `NaN` or `0`, which also catches `-0`. Host tracing for `random` is the existing seeded `Host::random`, and the pure test expects zero `host_futures`. Not re-run here.

EventSub. Source order matches the TypeScript helpers: exact `raid_direction === "outgoing"`, string fields require a non-empty trim and return the raw string, numeric fields accept a finite number or `Number(string)` and stop at the first success, booleans stop on the first real boolean, and cheer `bits` uses a typed number on `cheer.bits` before the top-level `bits` field. `safe_count` accepts only a non-array object whose field is a finite integer in `0..=2^53-1`. Tier normalization trims, lowercases, then drops JS whitespace, `_`, and `-`. `prime` is an exact normalized tier or a `plan` substring. `to_utf8` failure on an unpaired surrogate cannot equal the ASCII tier labels, so it takes the same default as a JS mismatch.

Replace. A JavaScript transcription of the KMP in `pure/strings.rs` matched `split`/`join` on the hand-picked UTF-16 and `$` cases and on 3,000 short fuzz inputs, including overlapping `aba` / `aaa`. Empty search returns the text after search, replacement, and text have been coerced. Replacement units are copied and not scanned. Quality executed the Rust function on the corpus replace cases; this transcription did not.

Registry and authority. `with_pure_builtins` installs the 27 corpus names and not the five context builtins. `redemption.input` is the same handler as `reward.input` with `alias_of`. `register` still replaces in place, keeps metadata when the new metadata is absent, and forces host dispatch. Vm order is evaluate arguments, missing-handler check, `minUserLevel` gate, then dispatch. Pure dispatch is a synchronous `fn`. The host arm is the only one that awaits. Pure handlers do not read or mint `effect_context`. Random increments `host_calls` and calls `host.random` only.

`value.rs` `js_string` / `nullish_string` / `parse_int` / `to_number` / `number_string` are unchanged versus the pre-get edit except the `get` compare above. Cycle and nullish joins observed in Node: `String(a)` for `a=[a]` is `""`, `String(['x', a, 'y'])` style `['x', cycle, 'y']` is `x,,y`, and `['x', null, undefined, 'y']` is `x,,,y`. Own `toString` of `null`, `3`, `undefined`, or the string `hello` all throw `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`. Own `valueOf: 3` without own `toString` is `[object Object]`. `checked_string` follows that split. `js_string` still does not.

## Scoped residuals

Non-iterable filter messages are outside the frozen corpus. Node `for (const c of 17)` throws `TypeError: 17 is not iterable`. `false` throws `TypeError: false is not iterable`. A plain object, including `{toString:null}`, throws `TypeError: {(intermediate value)} is not iterable`. `{toString:undefined}` throws `TypeError: object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))`. `pure/user.rs` returns `TypeError` / `name is not iterable` for every non-string, non-array name once a filter plan exists. The 4,694 cases include no expected `not iterable` text. The four non-string display cases are null, which is falsy and never iterated. Object messages are engine text, not a specified string. This is not a wrong successful value and not a 4,694 miss.

Unicode 16 base tables were not re-diffed scalar by scalar in this pass. ASCII fast-path gain and the Unicode regression gate belong to the lead benchmark still in progress. No production caller, deploy, or host-future wrapper was added in the reviewed diff.

The diff deletes the private `ASCII_CASING_FAST_PATH` toggle, the ASCII-only branches in lower, upper, and title, and the test loop that compared the fast and generic routes. What remains is the previous generic body:

- `lower` is `JsString::lower`, which lowercases each well-formed run and copies unpaired surrogates through unchanged (`value.rs`).
- `upper` uses the same run split, then `to_uppercase`, and copies each unpaired surrogate.
- `capitalize` uppercases only the first UTF-16 unit and copies the tail.
- `title` lowercases first, then uppercases a letter at a word start. Word starts use `js_compat::is_whitespace`. An unpaired surrogate does not start a word.
